title: How To Refocus Your Students Back On School
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Writing as students return from a year of pandemic disruption, Linsin argues against easing them back in gently and instead advocates pushing hard to refocus them right away. He identifies three drivers for this reset: a push for excellence that reignites motivation, a sense of purpose delivered through explicit why-questions attached to assignments, and genuine urgency communicated through the teacher's evident passion. He frames purpose as something that can operate at both the macro level of long-term goals and the micro level of a single day's lesson, arguing that without an explicit 'why,' students struggle to see the point of their work. The piece closes by tying these three elements — excellence, purpose, urgency — together as the combination needed to fully re-engage a demoralized, pandemic-affected class.
points: Pandemic-era standards have slipped, and the recommended response is to push hard immediately rather than ease students back in slowly.
A push for excellence in any pursuit is framed as motivationally activating on its own, regardless of the specific subject.
Purpose should be built into assignments explicitly by answering why the work matters and how it benefits the student.
Purpose can operate at both a macro (long-term goals) and micro (daily lesson) level, and its absence makes lessons feel pointless.
Genuine urgency, communicated through the teacher's visible passion, is the third necessary ingredient alongside excellence and purpose.
quotes: Over the past year, educational standards have fallen like a rodeo cowboy.
Here at SCM, however, we believe it’s best to get them right back up on the horse.
A push for excellence in anything , regardless of what it is, fires the motivational engines. It generates thoughts of the future, which is extraordinarily healthy to both body and mind.
Purpose is the driver for every worthy pursuit in our lives. Without it, there is nothing but empty entertainment and momentary pleasure.
Having purpose, even on a small scale, is highly motivational. Without the why it’s hard for students to see the point.
Together—excellence, purpose, urgency—will not only get your students back up on the horse, but galloping into their future.
